events.text: {npc} has walked up nine flights to the room you rent over the noodle shop, and has not mentioned the stairs once. {ctg_The} would be honoured, {he} says, to seat you among its External Elders. A good room. A stipend. The council, on the side nearest the door. "We would ask very little," {he} adds. In {his} experience, that sentence has never yet been true.

choices.text: Take the seat

effects.log: You sign. {npc} blots it with enormous care, the way one blots the name of something expensive.

choices.text: Thank {him}, and say you are not made for tables

ok.log: {npc} takes it well, and writes down every word on the stairs going back. It will be read aloud.

fail.log: You meant it kindly. It lands as a wanderer telling a nine-hundred-year-old house that it is a table.

choices.text: Tell {him} the room over the noodle shop suits you

effects.log: You say it with the window open. The whole street hears a great family turned down in favour of noodles, and {npc} has to walk back through them.

choices.text: Ask for a few years to think

effects.log: {npc} bows. "A few years," {he} says. {He} has the look of someone who can count.

events.text: You won the fight at Willow Crossing with nobody behind you, and within the month {npc} of {ctg_the} has found you drying your boots at a roadside shrine. {He} sits down on the wet step beside you in very good silk. "You have no banner," {he} says. "It must get tiring, being the only person who knows who you are. We could fix that by the spring."

choices.text: Let them fix it

effects.log: By spring you have a chair, a stipend, and a banner someone else has to carry. You had not known your shoulders were tired.

choices.text: Say the boots are nearly dry

effects.log: You put them on and walk. {npc} sits there a while longer in the wet, in the good silk, thinking about the look on your face.

choices.text: Say you will think about it on the road

effects.log: {npc} says the road is long, and that {ctg_the} has people all along it.

events.text: {npc} brings no gifts. {He} brings a list: the people who have been asking after you this year, and what they said. It is longer than you would have guessed and not very friendly. "Everyone alone looks like a meal, sooner or later," {he} says, folding it. "{ctg_The} keeps a seat for people who would prefer not to be eaten. External Elder. There are worse doors."

choices.text: Go through the door

effects.log: You move in with one bag. The list stops growing, and you do not ask {npc} how.

choices.text: Say you have always preferred to be hard to chew

ok.log: {npc} almost laughs, and leaves the list with you. You cannot tell whether that is a kindness.

fail.log: {npc} does not laugh. A name is added to the list, in front of you, in a very neat hand. It is yours.

choices.text: Put the list in the fire

effects.log: It burns well. {npc} watches it go with the air of someone who has copies.

events.text: The hall of {ctg_the} is the biggest room you have ever been asked into. {ctg_head} comes down three steps to meet you, which you learn afterward has not happened in eleven years, and {npc} stands behind {ctg_head} holding a robe in the colours of the house. The outsider's cut, with a narrow border. Forty people have stopped breathing to see if you will put your arms out.

choices.text: Put your arms out

effects.log: It fits. Of course it fits. They had your measure taken months ago, by someone you thought was selling you tea.

choices.text: Bow, and walk back out through forty people

effects.log: It is a very long room in that direction. {npc} is still holding the robe when you reach the doors.

choices.text: Bow, and ask leave to finish a vow first

effects.log: Nobody asks what vow. {ctg_head} goes back up the three steps, one at a time.

events.text: An old debt of yours has been bought. {npc} lays the paper on the table and does not ask for anything on it. "{ctg_The} paid this off last winter. No reason. We simply dislike seeing a person of your gifts inconvenienced." Then {he} mentions the elder's chair that has lately come free. {He} says the two things are not connected, and leaves a space for you to believe it.

choices.text: Take the chair and the paper

effects.log: You tear up the paper in {his} presence, which is what you were meant to do. It was a very good move, and you can admire it from your new room.

choices.text: Pay them back, to the last copper, and send it round

effects.log: It takes a while to find the silver, and you send it with no note. {npc} reads the empty note for a long time.

choices.text: Thank them, and leave the chair for someone who needs it

ok.log: {npc} tells {ctg_head} you were very polite. Nobody there is fooled, and nobody can quite complain.

fail.log: You said it as though {ctg_the} needed charity. {npc} repeats it word for word.

events.text: You have a place in the world already, and {npc} of {ctg_the} is careful to say so first. Nobody is asking you to leave anything. It is only that a chair in their hall has always been kept for a friend of the house, and it has stood empty since the last one died. There is silver with it each year. There is nothing to do. {He} says "nothing" very clearly.

choices.text: Let them keep the chair for you

effects.log: Your name goes up in a hall you will rarely see. The silver comes on time. Nothing has been asked for, yet.

choices.text: Say you could not sit in two places

ok.log: {npc} agrees that it is a pity, and writes something on {his} sleeve.

fail.log: You said it as if they had asked you to wash floors. {npc} writes something on {his} sleeve and presses quite hard.

choices.text: Ask who the last friend of the house was, and how they died

effects.log: {npc} tells you. It is a short story, and when it is over neither of you is pretending any more.

choices.text: Say you will think about it

effects.log: {npc} says the chair is patient. {He} says it the way one says a thing about a dog.

events.text: {npc} has come a long way to bring you a very small wooden tablet with your name on it. It would hang in the guest hall of {ctg_the}, among people who have done the house a kindness. You have not done the house a kindness. "Not yet," says {npc} pleasantly, and pours your tea for you in your own room.

choices.text: Take the tablet

effects.log: It goes up in the guest hall, in good company. Most of the names beside it have a line of small writing under them. Yours has room left.

choices.text: Hand it back, and pour {his} tea for {him}

effects.log: {npc} drinks it all, slowly, and bows, and takes the little tablet home in {his} sleeve to be shown to someone.

choices.text: Say to bring it back in a few years

effects.log: {npc} sets it on the shelf beside your door anyway. "To save me the carrying," {he} says.

events.text: At the Governor's banquet {ctg_head} makes a point of crossing the whole room to you, in front of everyone who matters, and calls you an old friend of the house, which is news to you. Everyone is listening. {npc}, at {ctg_head}'s elbow, murmurs the rest: a chair in their hall, in your honour, with a stipend. It would be so awkward to say anything but yes, in here.

choices.text: Say yes, in here

effects.log: The room relaxes. You have been put on a shelf in front of two hundred people. It is a very good shelf.

choices.text: Say you have never met, loudly enough

effects.log: The room does not relax. {ctg_head} smiles the whole way back across it, and you can feel the smile from where you stand.

choices.text: Make a joke of it, and change the subject to the wine

ok.log: They laugh, and you have said nothing at all. {npc} is not laughing. {He} knows what was just refused.

fail.log: The joke goes badly. It sounds exactly like what it is.

events.text: {npc} wishes to be frank. {ctg_The} is afraid of you. Not very, and not yet, but its people have started to count your years and your rungs. A chair in the hall would let them stop counting. It would let you stop being counted. "I would take it, in your place," {he} says. "I have seen what they do when they get tired of counting."

choices.text: Take it, and thank {him} for saying so

effects.log: You shake hands on it, which nobody in that house ever does. {npc} goes home looking as if a tooth has stopped hurting.

choices.text: Tell {him} to tell them to keep counting

effects.log: {npc} nods as though {he} expected nothing else. "I did say," {he} says, at the door, to nobody.

choices.text: Ask how long they can stand to wait

effects.log: "A few years," {npc} says. "After that it stops being my department."

events.text: {npc} has brought a scroll with a very long list of ancestors and, at the bottom of it, a living person of full age, who would be yours. An adult child of {ctg_head}, educated, unmarried, and said to be able to read a ledger upside down. {He} unrolls it across your table. It goes over the edge. "A marriage is the only treaty that has children," {he} says.

choices.text: Sign below the long list

effects.log: A date is set. You are about to find out what it is like to be related to all of that.

choices.text: Say you could not take a child of that house from it

ok.log: {npc} rolls the scroll back up, an inch at a time. {ctg_head} will be told you were overcome.

fail.log: There is a pause. "That is the first time," {npc} says, "anyone has told us our children are too good for them, and meant the opposite."

choices.text: Roll it up for {him}, and hand it back

effects.log: {npc} takes it. There is a person at the bottom of that scroll who will hear about this, and so will everyone that person grew up with.

choices.text: Ask for time, as one should

effects.log: The scroll stays with you for a season and then goes home. {npc} says these things should not be hurried, and looks at the calendar.

events.text: The person {ctg_the} wants you to marry has asked to see you first, which was not in the plan, and {npc} has plainly lost that argument. You meet in a garden, with {npc} standing just out of hearing and working hard at it. "They want me to tell you I am pleased," the heir says. "I am twenty-six and I have read your whole file. Ask me something."

choices.text: Ask what they want, and then say yes

effects.log: It is a long walk around that garden. You come out of it engaged and rather surprised, and {npc} looks at the two of you as if the plan has developed a crack.

choices.text: Ask what they want, and then say no

effects.log: "Thank you," says the heir quietly, and means it. {ctg_head} does not. {npc} will be the one to carry that home.

choices.text: Say this should not be settled in a garden

effects.log: The heir nods. "No," they say. "It is usually settled in a ledger. Come back when you know which you want."

events.text: A matchmaker of {ctg_the}, with {npc} carrying her boxes, has spread three painted portraits on your floor: three grown cousins of the name, of the sort of ages that will not raise an eyebrow, each described in beautiful handwriting. {npc} coughs. The fourth box holds what the house would settle on you on the day, and someone has taken care to leave the lid off it.

choices.text: Point at one, and close the lid

effects.log: The matchmaker claps twice. The whole thing takes less time than buying a horse, and you have the odd sense you were the one being looked at.

choices.text: Close the lid, and hand her back all three

effects.log: She packs them up with her lips together. She has made nine hundred marriages and she knows exactly how this will be told.

choices.text: Compliment all three at great length, and choose none

ok.log: She is delighted with you. It takes her until she is home to work out what you did.

fail.log: She is not delighted with you. "Is it the noses?" she asks, for the whole street to hear.

events.text: You should know why they are asking, says {npc}, who has had some wine. {ctg_The} marries what it cannot beat. It has done so for six hundred years. It is a very happy family, full of people like you, who have all learned to sit in the side rooms. Then {he} puts down the cup, straightens up and offers you a named adult of the house, in perfect form.

choices.text: Accept in perfect form

effects.log: {npc} looks at you for some time. "Well," {he} says. "I did tell you." {He} seems to like you for it.

choices.text: Decline in perfect form

effects.log: You both bow. It is the most honest conversation either of you will have this year, and it has made you enemies anyway.

choices.text: Ask {him} to come back sober

effects.log: {npc} says that {he} will. {He} says it will not be nearly as much fun.

events.text: {ctg_head} writes to you personally. The letter says that your house and theirs would make a fine thing together, and it names someone of the blood, grown and capable, who has agreed. {npc}, who brought it, adds that the offer is good for as long as it takes {him} to finish this cup. {He} drinks slowly. {He} is a kind person, and {he} has been told not to be.

choices.text: Pour {him} another cup, and say yes

effects.log: You drink to it together. By the time the cup is empty you have in-laws. There are a very great number of them.

choices.text: Let {him} finish the cup

effects.log: {He} finishes it, and sets it upside down on your table. In that house, it is how you mark a door.

choices.text: Send back a letter as fine as theirs

ok.log: It takes you three drafts. {ctg_head} reads it twice, admires it, and does not forgive you.

fail.log: It took you three drafts, and it shows. {ctg_head} has it read aloud at dinner.

events.text: Spring at the Lantern Fair. A person of {ctg_the}, grown and sharp-eyed, has been put beside you at every stall for three days now by accident. On the third evening {npc} appears at your elbow and asks how you have found the fair. Everyone in the street knows what is being asked. So does the one with the sharp eyes, who is looking at a lantern with terrible concentration.

choices.text: Say you have found it very good, and that you will speak to the house

effects.log: The lantern gets bought. It is the worst lantern on the street. It is still in the house when you are old.

choices.text: Say you are leaving in the morning

effects.log: You leave in the morning. A sharp-eyed person of good family has been made a fool of at a fair, and the fair will remember for years.

choices.text: Say it is a long fair

effects.log: {npc} agrees that it is. There will be another next year, and one after. {He} does not look like someone with nothing else to do.

events.text: The first cart is ginseng. The second is bolts of southern silk. The third is a very good horse that bites. {npc} of {ctg_the} rides at the back of them and says there is nothing to sign. It is merely that the house likes to see its friends well supplied. You had not known you were a friend. Now half the province has seen the carts.

choices.text: Keep the carts

effects.log: It is all excellent. Even the horse. Half the province has noted down whose friend you are now.

choices.text: Send every cart back, with the horse

effects.log: They go back down the road in a long line, in full daylight. {npc} rides at the front of them this time, with a face like a shut door.

choices.text: Keep the horse, and return the rest with thanks

ok.log: It is the sort of answer nobody can quite be offended by, and they are, a little.

fail.log: The horse bites {npc} on the way out, and you laugh. That was a mistake.

events.text: {npc} is holding a sword in both hands. It is older than the Empire and nobody has been able to say who made it. {ctg_The} has kept it in a sealed room for three hundred years and now it would like you to have it, for no reason at all. {He} would like you to know exactly how many people would kill for it. {He} has brought the list.

choices.text: Take it

effects.log: It sits in the hand as if it has been waiting. You will never be able to draw it without someone remembering where it came from.

choices.text: Tell {him} a gift like that has a very long handle

effects.log: {npc} wraps it up again, with care. {He} will remember that about the handle, and repeat it, and not for fun.

choices.text: Say you could not accept it yet

effects.log: It goes back in the sealed room. {npc} says the room can wait. {He} is looking at your hands when {he} says it.

events.text: Your rent has been paid, ten years ahead. So has your tailor. Someone has quietly settled up with the old woman who sells you medicine, and she has begun to bow to you. When you go looking, you find {npc} of {ctg_the} eating dumplings on your step. "We hear things are dear this year," {he} says. "Dumpling?"

choices.text: Have a dumpling

effects.log: They are very good. You finish the plate together and nobody says what has happened, and it has happened.

choices.text: Pay it all back, and put the receipts in {his} bowl

effects.log: It costs you, and it is worth it. {npc} reads each one, chewing. "They told me you were proud," {he} says. "I said that would be cheaper."

choices.text: Have a dumpling, and tell {him} that this does not count

ok.log: "Of course not," says {npc}, delighted, and writes down that you said so.

fail.log: "Of course not," says {npc}, not delighted, and goes home with the plate.

events.text: A manual comes, in a plain box. Not a great one, or not quite, but it has been copied out by someone who understood it, and in the margins someone has answered the exact question you have been stuck on for six years. {npc} of {ctg_the} would like you to know they read your last three fights very closely. {He} says it as a compliment, and it is one. It is also the other thing.

choices.text: Keep it, and read it twice

effects.log: The answer in the margin is right. You are grateful, and you are also a person whose stuck places are known to {ctg_the}.

choices.text: Send it back unread

effects.log: That is the hardest thing you have done this year, and nobody will ever know how hard. {npc} will only know you sent it back.

choices.text: Leave it shut on the table, and ask for time

effects.log: It stays shut on the table for one evening, which is as long as you can bear to have it there, and then {npc} takes it away again.

events.text: They have sent a doctor. An excellent one, to look at that old wound you thought nobody knew about, and {npc} of {ctg_the} waits in the next room while it is done. It does feel better. It feels better than it has in fifteen years. The doctor mentions, packing up, that she will need to come twice a year from now on, as long as the house is happy.

choices.text: Thank her, and ask when she is coming next

effects.log: You sleep through the night for the first time since you can remember. {npc} sends a note hoping that you are well. It is a very short note.

choices.text: Thank her, and say she need not come again

effects.log: She looks at you with real regret, and tells you how to manage it alone. {npc} carries the answer home. The wound aches by winter.

choices.text: Ask her to teach you to do it yourself

ok.log: She laughs, and does, and it is the one thing the house did not mean to give you. {npc} takes that home as well.

fail.log: She is not allowed to, she says. She looks frightened to have been asked.

events.text: You belong to nobody, which {npc} of {ctg_the} says is a wonderful thing, like a good sword lying in the road. Nobody would ask you to join anything. They would only like it known that you stand with them, as a friend, with a letter that opens their doors in nine provinces. And a little silver each year to walk through them on.

choices.text: Take the letter

effects.log: Doors open. They had always been there, you realise, and you had always been outside them.

choices.text: Tell {him} a sword in the road belongs to nobody

effects.log: "Until someone picks it up," says {npc}. {He} does not stop smiling on the way out, and that is the worst of it.

choices.text: Say you will think about it on the road

effects.log: {npc} says that is the only place you ever seem to think.

events.text: {npc} has found out where you sleep, and is sitting there. It is not a threat, {he} says. {ctg_The} would prefer that a person of your weight was on a list of friends. There are only two lists. {He} says this without any heat, and offers you a pear.

choices.text: Take the pear, and the list

effects.log: It is a very good pear. Your name goes on the shorter list, and the silver starts to arrive.

choices.text: Say you have never been able to read lists

ok.log: It gets a real laugh out of {npc}. {He} leaves you the pear. Your name goes on the other list, but in pencil.

fail.log: {npc} does not laugh. {He} takes the pear back, and {he} finishes it on the way out.

choices.text: Ask {him} to get off your bed

effects.log: {He} gets off your bed, and straightens the blanket. "I did ask nicely," {he} says.

events.text: There is a war coming between {ctg_the} and {ctg_rival}, says {npc}. Not soon. But everyone is choosing their friends for it now, while they are cheap. You are not cheap, {he} wishes to say, and {he} names a figure each year for simply being known to prefer one side. You would not have to do a thing. Until you did.

choices.text: Let it be known

effects.log: It is known by evening, on both sides. You have been paid to have an opinion, and you are going to have to keep it.

choices.text: Say both of them can have their war without you

effects.log: {npc} sighs. "That is what we will tell them you said," {he} says. "They will both hear it as the other side's answer."

choices.text: Say it is early to be choosing

effects.log: {npc} agrees that it is early. {He} says prices only go one way.

events.text: You hold a rank under someone else's banner, and {npc} of {ctg_the} is too well bred to ask you to leave it. An understanding is all they want: a friend in that hall, who would hear things first, and be remembered at the New Year. Nothing that would look like anything. "And when you rise," {he} says, "you will have rather more friends than the people above you."

choices.text: Come to an understanding

effects.log: You have a friend at {ctg_the} and a stipend you do not mention at home. Nobody here has noticed, as far as you know.

choices.text: Tell {him} you will report that {he} came

effects.log: {npc} is not at all worried. "Do," {he} says. "I would like to know how much of that hall already knows." You find out it is rather a lot.

choices.text: Say your oath has no room for a second friend

ok.log: {npc} bows, as one does to a good answer. It is a good answer. {He} would have preferred to have you.

fail.log: {npc} asks, gently, which oath, and quotes it to you. You have misremembered it. {He} leaves you with that.

events.text: {npc} wants to give you something that your own elders will not. A real place at the table of {ctg_the} whenever you are in their country; a say, however small, in things your own house will never let you near. {He} knows exactly how high you have got and exactly how high they mean to let you. {He} tells you both numbers. {He} is not wrong about either.

choices.text: Sit at their table too

effects.log: Their table is very good. You go home to your own and find you are looking at it differently.

choices.text: Tell {him} your own table is enough

effects.log: You say it firmly. It may even be true. {npc} goes home with the numbers still in {his} head and with your name beside them.

choices.text: Ask how long that seat stays open

effects.log: {npc} says it depends how fast you rise. {He} says it as a compliment, and leaves.

events.text: A letter has reached you past your own gate, which is not easy. {npc} of {ctg_the} has heard that you are being passed over, and thinks it is a great shame. If you were to speak for their house in the coming council, as anyone might, there would be someone waiting to speak for you. {He} has signed it, which is either very brave or very well thought through.

choices.text: Speak for them, as anyone might

effects.log: You speak. It goes the way they wanted. Someone you have never met starts saying your name in rooms you have never seen.

choices.text: Burn it, and tell {him} so

effects.log: You write back a single line. {npc} keeps it. In that house, they keep everything.

events.text: You have a house of your own, and {npc} of {ctg_the} addresses you as one head of a house to another, which {ctg_head} has told {him} to do and which still seems to hurt a little. They propose a friendship: open roads, shared word of trouble, a yearly exchange of gifts in which theirs would be somewhat larger. And each would stand with the other, should anyone ever be so foolish.

choices.text: Set your seal to it

effects.log: Your name goes up beside theirs. Those you lead stand a little straighter, and you are now in a very old quarrel that you had not heard of.

choices.text: Say your people have only just learned to stand alone

ok.log: {npc} says that it is a fine thing to be able to say. {ctg_head} will be told you are proud, which they had supposed.

fail.log: {npc} asks how many of your people, exactly. {He} seems to know.

choices.text: Say no house of yours will stand behind {ctg_the}

effects.log: You have made a rather good speech. {npc} has a good memory. Your people cheer, and that, too, will get back.

events.text: {npc} has come with a proposal that makes you the younger brother, in the politest possible way. Your house would keep its name. {ctg_The} would keep an eye on it. Their people would train yours, and yours would be sent to them at the proper age. There would be silver. A lot of houses your size have made this bargain, and {he} can name them, and they still exist.

choices.text: Take the bargain

effects.log: Their teachers come in the spring. They are good. Your people learn quickly, and they learn who taught them.

choices.text: Ask {him} to name the ones who said no

effects.log: {He} names two. It does not take long. You thank {him}, and {he} leaves you to look at the walls you built.

choices.text: Say you will put it before your people

effects.log: {npc} says of course you will. {He} says it as one who knows who decides things in a house.

events.text: A branch of your people is in trouble with its neighbours, and suddenly {npc} of {ctg_the} is there with soldiers, silver and a settlement, all of which you would have asked for if you had known. {He} does not ask for thanks. {He} asks only for a standing friendship, in writing, so that the next time {he} will not have to hurry. It is very hard to say no to someone who has just saved your people.

choices.text: Write it down

effects.log: It is written. Nobody asks whether the trouble was an accident, and you find you are not asking either.

choices.text: Thank {him}, and pay for the soldiers

effects.log: You pay in full, and it costs. It is the most insulting thing you could do, and {npc} knows it, and thanks you.

choices.text: Ask {him} how {he} knew in time

ok.log: {npc} tells you the truth, or something shaped like it, and lets the writing wait for now. You will not get a better answer.

fail.log: {npc} is hurt, and it is beautifully done. By evening your own people are asking why you were rude to the one who saved them.

events.text: The heads of the great houses do not usually send envoys to the palace: they send apologies. So {npc} of {ctg_the}, in the audience hall, with your guards all around {him}, has come a long way to say something new. {ctg_The} would support your claim, openly, with its name and its fighters, against anyone in the jianghu. It asks a seat at the edge of your council. It asks that a few old laws be forgotten.

choices.text: Forget a few laws

effects.log: Their banner goes up beside yours at the spring rites. The Censorate loses a file. You have an army you do not pay for and a guest you cannot ask to go.

choices.text: Remind {him} who sits on this side of the hall

effects.log: Your guards shift their feet at the tone. {npc} knocks {his} head on the floor the correct number of times, and it does not look like fear.

choices.text: Have {him} wait outside the gate

effects.log: {He} waits. {He} is still there at the first snow. The court starts to talk about it, and you begin to see that this was the point.

events.text: {npc} lays out the map on the floor of your study. Your tax roads run through three provinces where nothing moves unless {ctg_the} allows it. They have always allowed it. They would like to go on allowing it, as friends, with a modest title for {ctg_head} and an arrangement over salt. {He} does not mention what the roads would look like without the arrangement. {He} just leaves the map.

choices.text: Grant the title, and the salt

effects.log: The roads go on moving. You have paid a tax to your own taxpayers, and the treasury sends you a note that it is delighted.

choices.text: Offer the title, and keep the salt

ok.log: {npc} takes the title. You will hear about the salt.

fail.log: {npc} regrets to say that the title was never what they wanted.

choices.text: Roll up the map, and give it back

effects.log: {npc} takes it. Your ministers look at the floor, where it was. Every one of them has family in those provinces.

events.text: There is a great wedding coming, at {ctg_the}, and {npc} has come with the invitation: you are not asked to attend it. You are asked to sanctify it, with your seal, as a friend of the house. It would make their claims on three other families a matter of imperial record. In return they would stop telling anyone what they know about the last census. {He} smiles, and folds {his} hands.

choices.text: Bring out the seal

effects.log: Your seal goes down. It is a very fine wedding, and nobody there looks directly at you. The last census is never spoken of again.

choices.text: Tell {him} to go ahead and tell them about the census

effects.log: You wait for it all winter. When it comes, you are ready, and it is still not pleasant.

events.text: {npc} is back. {He} has got a little older and is carrying the same offer, and {he} has not sat down yet. "You said a few years," {he} says. "{ctg_The} has counted them, on your behalf. {ctg_head} asks me to say the offer stands, and that this is the last time anyone will say so." {He} takes a pinch of snuff, and waits.

choices.text: Say yes

effects.log: It has been waiting for you the whole time, every line of it. They do not even have to change the date on it by much.

choices.text: Say no

effects.log: It is not a surprise to anyone by now. {npc} has had years to work out what {he} will say at home, and {he} goes to say it.

events.text: Every year you did not answer, {npc} says, somebody at {ctg_the} moved a small stone across a board. There is now a row of them. {ctg_head} has taken to looking at it during meals. {He} tells you this as a friend, {he} says. And so, with what everyone has come to think of as great patience, is what you were offered: yes or no.

choices.text: Yes

effects.log: You watch {him} let out a breath {he} has been holding for some time. Somewhere a row of small stones gets swept into a box.

choices.text: No

effects.log: {npc} nods. Somewhere a row of small stones gets moved to a different board.

events.text: You had nearly forgotten. {npc} had not. {He} finds you on the way out of the bathhouse, of all places, and falls into step without a word for some way. "I have told them you were thinking," {he} says at last. "I have told them that for a long time now. I would take it as a kindness if you would tell me what you thought."

choices.text: Tell {him} yes

effects.log: {He} stops walking and bows, right there in the road, in front of the fishmonger. You think {he} is honestly glad.

choices.text: Tell {him} no, and buy {him} a drink first

ok.log: {He} drinks, you keep to tea, and you tell {him} over the second cup. {He} thanks you for the wine. It will not save anything, but {he} remembers it.

fail.log: You tell {him} over the second cup. {He} leaves the cup full.

choices.text: Tell {him} no, right there

effects.log: {He} stops walking. You go on. It is a while before you hear {him} start again, in the other direction.

events.text: The carts of {ctg_the} come up the road with gifts for someone. You stand aside in the mud to let them by, with your bundle, looking like what you look like. The envoy on the lead horse asks you the way to the house of a master, whom you beat, once, on a bridge, a long time ago. They are half of what you are. You are holding the reins of a mule.

choices.text: Point the way

effects.log: You point. The envoy tosses you a coin for it. You keep the coin. It is a very good coin, and it is the only thing that house will ever give you.

choices.text: Let the envoy feel who they asked

effects.log: The lead horse stops of its own accord. By the time the envoy has got down, the carts have turned round in the road. You have a lot of explaining to expect, and a lot of carts.

events.text: There is a list going round the teahouse: who {ctg_the} is courting this year. Everybody has a view. You hear the third-best sabre in the county named, and a retired general, and a youth who won one duel. A man at your table reads it aloud and asks what you think, as a person who has clearly never been on any list in your life.

choices.text: Say it sounds like a good list

effects.log: He agrees, and buys you a cup out of pity. It is restful, being pitied. Nobody has ever tried to marry you off for it.

choices.text: Set down your cup, and let the room know what is sitting in it

effects.log: The man stops reading. So does the teahouse. Someone is running up the road toward {ctg_the} before your cup stops ringing.

events.text: A matchmaker of {ctg_the} has come to the inn with her boxes for the young fighter in the next room, who is a nice enough child. On the way past your door she gives you the look that is kept for furniture, and asks you to move your feet. You move them. Through the wall you hear her describing the fortune that goes with the match, in round numbers.

choices.text: Go back to your soup

effects.log: It is decent soup. There is nobody coming through that door to tell you how lucky you are. You find you can taste it.

choices.text: Knock on the wall, once

effects.log: It is only a small knock. The wall cracks from the floor to the rafters, and on the other side of it a very experienced matchmaker stops talking and begins to count again.

events.text: {npc} does not sit down this time. {ctg_The} has a quarrel with {ctg_rival} over a river crossing, and it is about to be settled at dawn on the east bank. You owe nothing, {he} says, of course. Only, your name has been on their letters for some time, and everyone on the east bank has read them. {He} has brought a horse.

choices.text: Get on the horse

effects.log: You stand on the east bank at dawn. It goes the way a thing goes when you stand on that side of it. People you have never met will know your face now, and not fondly.

choices.text: Say you are not able to come, this time

effects.log: {npc} nods and takes the horse away. You watch it go. The east bank is settled without you, and somebody makes a note.

choices.text: Say you never agreed to any river

effects.log: "You agreed to all the rivers," says {npc}. "That is what it was." {He} is quite white. {He} says {he} will tell them.

events.text: A disciple of {ctg_rival} has been found on land belonging to {ctg_the}, and it has gone the way those things go. There is to be a meeting of arms in the matter, with friends on both sides, and your name was called out for their side before anyone asked you. {npc} says {he} regrets that. {He} has also brought you the names of who you will be fighting.

choices.text: Read the names, and go

effects.log: You go and you win, and one of the names does not get up for a long time. On the way home you try to remember what it was about, and you find you cannot.

choices.text: Send a note that you are unwell

effects.log: You send it. You are in excellent health, and the whole jianghu knows that. {npc} delivers the note with a straight face.

choices.text: Tell {him} to cross your name off

effects.log: {npc} says it has already been read aloud. {He} will see what can be crossed. You will not like what {he} crosses instead.

events.text: Someone has burned a storehouse of {ctg_the}. Nobody can prove it was {ctg_rival}, and so {ctg_head} would like someone who is not of the house to go and speak to them about it. Someone with your reputation. It would not take a long conversation. {npc} is looking at the wall above your head while {he} says this.

choices.text: Go and have the conversation

effects.log: It is not a long conversation. You leave a very frightened steward, an upturned table and a clear impression. It is also your impression, not theirs. That was the idea.

choices.text: Say that you do not do errands of that kind

effects.log: {npc} looks at the wall a little longer. "No," {he} says. "It is only that we had thought you did."

choices.text: Ask {him} to stop looking at the wall, and tell {ctg_head} you are finished

effects.log: {npc} looks at you, at last. "That was what I was afraid of," {he} says, and {he} seems to mean it.

events.text: Two of the young of {ctg_the} have got themselves shut up in a fort by {ctg_rival}, in a dispute over some salt. {npc} has come by night. There is no one else who could reach them in time, {he} says, and this one is real: {he} is not smiling, and {he} has ridden a horse to death. They are twenty and twenty-two. Behind that wall they are just two frightened people.

choices.text: Go tonight

effects.log: You bring them out alive through a broken wall. Their mother will never speak to you about it, and she sends a jar of pickled plums each year until she dies. The fort's commander does not get over it either.

choices.text: Tell {him} you cannot, and mean it

effects.log: {npc} does not argue. {He} gets on another horse. You hear about the two of them in the spring.

events.text: There is a hearing, in the matter of some property. All {ctg_the} needs is for you to say that you were present on a certain night in a certain place and saw a certain thing. You were not there. Nobody will suppose you were, but they will suppose you are too large to contradict. {npc} has written it out for you, with the difficult words spelled.

choices.text: Say it, in a clear voice

effects.log: You say it. The property changes hands. The old man who lost it looks at you all the way out of the room, and you have a very good memory for faces, as it happens.

choices.text: Say you have no memory of that night

effects.log: It is technically true. {npc} sighs. The hearing goes on without you, and it goes badly for them, and they know whose memory to thank.

choices.text: Read it out in the hall, and say who wrote it

effects.log: You read it out, in a clear voice, with the spelling. There is a silence. The old man begins to laugh. {npc} closes {his} eyes.

events.text: {ctg_head} would like your name on a letter. It says that a certain person of {ctg_rival} is a liar and a coward, and has been saying things about the house. You have met this person once. They were perfectly pleasant. But a letter with your name on it would be read to the end, says {npc}, and {he} would not be asking otherwise.

choices.text: Sign it

effects.log: You sign. It is read to the end, in a great many places. That perfectly pleasant person writes to you only once, to ask why. You do not answer.

choices.text: Say your hand is too poor for fine letters

effects.log: It is an old excuse. They have seen your hand. {npc} takes the letter back, and finds another name, smaller than yours.

choices.text: Write to that person yourself, and warn them

effects.log: You do. They write back to thank you, and to say the letter has already gone round. {npc} has read your note, too. Of course {he} has.

events.text: A marriage between {ctg_the} and another house is coming apart, and someone is needed to tell the other side, with authority, that the bride's health is excellent. It is not. It is in fact the point. {npc} would not trouble you, except that you have been seen with the doctor. {He} lets you think about who saw you, and why.

choices.text: Tell them it is excellent

effects.log: The marriage goes ahead. You are at the wedding, and you are very well treated. It is the kind of thing that keeps you up later on.

choices.text: Say you know nothing about medicine

effects.log: It is a poor answer and everyone knows it. The marriage falls through in the end. {npc} tells you that you are not to blame, and writes that down too.

events.text: They only want your name. {ctg_The} is opening a new trade road, through country that belongs to {ctg_rival}, and it would go easier if the first caravan flew your colours alongside theirs. You do not have to be there. {npc} says that you never have to be there, that is what is so restful about it. Everyone along the road will just assume you are.

choices.text: Lend your colours

effects.log: They fly over nine hundred miles of someone else's road. By the end of the year people you have never met are afraid of you, for things you did not do.

choices.text: Say your colours are not for hire

effects.log: You have never been so dignified. {npc} folds up the sketch of your banner. {He} had already had it sewn.

choices.text: Tell {him} to take your name off everything

effects.log: "Everything," {npc} repeats. {He} takes out a very long list and starts reading it to you. It takes a while. You had not known.

events.text: A young person of {ctg_the} needs a teacher, for a year, for reasons nobody will explain. A very specific sort of teacher: one whose name would keep {ctg_rival} from coming after them. They have sent the young person already. They are sitting at your gate, on a box. {npc} says they will be no trouble, and {he} leaves before you can answer.

choices.text: Open the gate

effects.log: It is a difficult year. The young person is not what you were told, and they are hiding from something real. Men of {ctg_rival} come to the gate twice, and you meet them there.

choices.text: Leave them on the box, and send word to {ctg_head}

effects.log: It rains. On the third day someone comes for the box and the person on it. Nobody says anything, and it gets around.

events.text: {ctg_head} would like you at the New Year, standing where {ctg_rival} can see you. That is all. You need only stand there, in a good robe, for the length of a banquet, and be seen to laugh at one joke. {npc} has brought the robe, and a note of which joke. It is not a very good joke.

choices.text: Stand there, and laugh

effects.log: You laugh at exactly the right time. All down the far side of the hall, faces close. Somewhere in that row there is someone who will remember the sound.

choices.text: Be somewhere else at the New Year

effects.log: You spend it on a mountain with a cold dumpling. It is the best New Year you have had in years, and it will cost you.

events.text: {npc} is sitting in the shade of your own gate. {He} is of {ctg_rival}, or was close to someone who was. You stood on the wrong side of a river, {he} says, and you have probably forgotten. {He} has not come to fight today. {He} only wanted to see your face, so {he} would know it later. {He} has seen it, thank you.

choices.text: Ask what you did

effects.log: {He} tells you. It takes some time. You did not know any of the people in it. That seems to be what {he} finds hardest.

choices.text: Settle it now, in the road

roll.foeName: an enemy with a long memory

ok.log: It does not take long. {He} goes down in the dust, in front of your gate, and that is one less person who knows your face. Others do.

fail.log: {He} is better than {he} looked. {He} steps back and bows, with skinned knuckles, and goes on up the road.

events.text: A cup arrives at your table with the compliments of {npc}. You can't place the name. It is a good wine, and has nothing in it. {He} sends one every month now, wherever you are, to every town, without a note. It is the business with {ctg_the}, of course, and the people on the other side of it, and {he} wants you to know how easily {he} could have done otherwise.

choices.text: Send a cup back

effects.log: You send one back, of your own, and it has nothing in it either. This goes on for some years. It is the longest conversation you have with anyone in that time.

choices.text: Find {him}, and tell {him} to stop

effects.log: You find {him} in a wine shop. {He} says of course, and thanks you for coming. The cups stop. Now there is nothing to tell you where {he} is.

events.text: Your name has been cut into a bridge post on the road to {ctg_rival}, with a line through it. Then another. By the time you are through that country you have counted thirty. A woodcutter tells you that a person named {npc} does it, going ahead of you by a day. {He} is not hiding. {He} has just never yet been where you are.

choices.text: Catch {him} up

ok.log: You catch {him} with the knife in {his} hand, at the thirty-first post. There is a long moment. {He} goes on cutting, and you find you have nothing to say. You add the line yourself.

fail.log: You never do catch up. The posts go on as far as the border, in a very steady hand.

choices.text: Leave them, and let the road talk

effects.log: You pass the posts as if they were posts. People notice that as well.

events.text: They return your things, which you had not known they had. A boy brings them: a borrowed book, a letter from thirty years ago, a good knife you lost. {npc} comes behind and stands at the gate for a while without coming in. Nobody at {ctg_the} will use your name again, {he} says, except for one purpose. {He} says that {he} had hoped, personally. Then {he} goes.

choices.text: Keep the knife

effects.log: You keep the knife. It has been sharpened, by someone who wanted you to know that they could get at it.

choices.text: Send it all back after {him}

effects.log: The boy has a heavy walk home. It is a poor thing to do to a boy, and you give him something for it.

choices.text: Stand at the gate until {he} is out of sight

effects.log: It is a long road, and you see all of it. {npc} does not look round. You had thought {he} might.

events.text: The stipend stops. The doors of {ctg_the} in nine provinces close, one a month, each with a small polite note. {npc} writes the notes. You come to know {his} hand well. The last one says only that {ctg_head} has asked for your name to be taken down from the hall, and that it took two men, because whoever put it up had used good nails.

choices.text: Frame the note

effects.log: It hangs by your door. Visitors ask about it, and you tell them. It does you no harm at all, and it does not do you any good.

choices.text: Burn the whole packet

effects.log: They burn well, and you feel nothing, which is about what they were for.

events.text: {npc} has brought a ledger and {he} opens it on your table. Every call {ctg_the} has made on you is written in it, with what you did. {He} draws a line under the last of them, in red, and turns the book around so that you can see. "We have never done this before," {he} says. "They usually die." {He} seems rather pleased. You have your own name back. They would still come if you called.

choices.text: Ask for the page

effects.log: {He} cuts it out with a small knife and gives it to you. There are people in that page. You read their names once and put it where you keep such things.

choices.text: Thank {him}, and pour

effects.log: You drink to the line in red. It is the first time the two of you have sat down with nothing to ask, and it turns out you do not have much to say. You do it anyway.

events.text: A cart comes up from {ctg_the}. It has nothing on it but a small jar, and {npc} driving. The jar holds salt, from the table of {ctg_head}, the sort that is given to those who have eaten there and owe nothing and are owed nothing. It is, you are told, very rare. Nobody has ever been sure what you do with it. {npc} recommends fish.

choices.text: Have fish

effects.log: It is excellent fish. You and {npc} eat it on the cart, and {he} tells you several things that {he} no longer has any reason not to tell you.

choices.text: Keep it on the shelf, and leave it sealed

effects.log: It stays on the shelf. Any visitor who knows what it is looks at it and then looks at you, and speaks a little more carefully.

events.text: {npc} is quite young, for someone sent by {ctg_the}, and {he} has a list of the gifts that the house has sent you over the years, from before {he} was born. You had forgotten most of them. "My grandmother carried the second one," {he} says. There is another cart outside. {He} has been told to say it is the finest yet. It is much the same. Most things are, after the first hundred years.

choices.text: Keep the cart, and ask after the grandmother

effects.log: You knew her, it turns out. You tell {him} a story about her which {he} has never heard, and that is the only thing in this whole exchange that was worth anything.

choices.text: Tell {him} you have enough carts

effects.log: You say it kindly, and it is not taken kindly. {He} will have to go home and tell them that you have stopped wanting things, and they find that very frightening.

choices.text: Tell {him} to come back when {he} is older

effects.log: {He} laughs, and then {he} sees that you mean it, and {he} stops.

events.text: They have sent a very rare thing, from {ctg_the}: a letter you wrote yourself, a hundred years ago, to someone who is long dead. You had forgotten that you ever felt that way about anything. {npc} says nothing. It has been kept with care, in a box, and the box is yours as well. They have kept the rest of them too, and there are a good many. They would be so pleased to go on keeping them.

choices.text: Take the box, and let them keep the rest

effects.log: You read it that night, by yourself. It is very badly written. You are not going to be able to refuse that house much, now, and they know it.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to burn the rest, or use them

effects.log: They may do what they like. You are older than anyone it could shame. {npc} bows, and {he} does not know what to do with {his} face.

events.text: The chair {ctg_the} has kept for friends of the house has had nine people in it since you were first asked, {npc} tells you. You have been to most of the funerals. It would mean something to the young, {he} says, to have someone in it who remembers why the house was ever worth being friends with. It is a very good chair. {He} looks about nineteen to you. They all do, these days.

choices.text: Sit in it, then

effects.log: It is the same chair. You remember when it was new. The young come and look at you, and you tell them which of their ancestors could not hold their drink.

choices.text: Say you have buried enough of its people

effects.log: You have, and {npc} knows it. {He} goes home with that. You had not meant it to be a threat, and you can hear that it was.

choices.text: Say to ask you again in a few years

effects.log: {npc} says that {he} will. You will both know by then which of you was joking.

events.text: It is the fourth time that a person of {ctg_the} has climbed up here to ask you this, and the first three are dead. {npc} has all of their notes. It seems that you have a way of saying no which each of them described quite differently. {He} would like you to know that {he} has read them. {He} has brought a very small gift, some of your favourite tea, which you stopped drinking sixty years ago.

choices.text: Drink it, and say yes, for the other three

effects.log: It is not as good as you remember. Nothing is. It is a pleasant thing, all the same, to be somebody's fourth attempt.

choices.text: Tell {him} how you would have said no to the others

ok.log: You do all three voices. {He} is delighted, and {he} writes it down, and it is still a no.

fail.log: You do all three voices. {He} does not laugh. {He} knew one of them rather well.

choices.text: Say what you said to the first one

effects.log: You remember it word for word, and it still works. {He} shuts {his} notes.

events.text: {ctg_The} has a grown child of the house, sensible and of good age, and it wishes to offer a match, and {npc} is too well bred to mention the difference in your years. The person in question is not. "You knew my great-grandmother," they say, sitting down across from you, with a very direct look. "I am told she thought you were a fool. I would like to find out for myself. And I would like the library."

choices.text: Tell them they can have the library

effects.log: It is not like anything else you have done lately. You had forgotten that a person can be surprised at your age. They get the library, and they are right about most of it.

choices.text: Say that you have buried enough of the ones you married

effects.log: It is true, and they do not argue. {npc} takes them home. You sit for a while, with the library.

choices.text: Say you would like to think about it, and mean it

effects.log: They look at you for a while. "How long does that take, for you?" they ask. It is a fair question.

events.text: {npc} has brought the marriage scroll of {ctg_the}. It has your name on it already: not this time, but a long way up, in an old hand, and crossed out. Somebody offered you this once before, and you said no, or you said yes and it ended. You honestly cannot recall. The person at the bottom of the scroll, grown and capable, is six generations down from that. Someone in that house has a sense of humour.

choices.text: Sign below the crossed-out one

effects.log: You put your name there, under your name. It makes the whole of the house very happy. You will have to ask someone what happened the last time.

choices.text: Ask to see who it was that you turned down

ok.log: {npc} shows you. You look for a long time. You thank {him}, and you give {him} back the scroll, and {he} sees that it would be no use.

fail.log: You have no memory of that person. {npc} can see that. It will be told in that house for a very long time.

choices.text: Cross yourself out again

effects.log: There is a pen on the table. You do it neatly, under the first one. {npc} takes the scroll away, holding it level, so that it can dry.

events.text: {npc} has been a long time finding you, because you have not been anyone for quite a while. {ctg_The} has need of a person who has seen what you have seen. They do not care about your banner, which you never had. An External Elder, with a room with a stove. {He} looks at your hut, and at your hands. "You must have seen every kind of house there is," {he} says. "Would you not like to sit down in one?"

choices.text: Sit down in it

effects.log: You had not known you were cold. It is a good stove. You will have to learn all their names, and then, in time, their children's.

choices.text: Say you have seen every kind of house

effects.log: You have. You saw what happened to the last one that asked. {npc} looks around the hut one more time, and {he} is frightened of it now.

choices.text: Say you might, when the winter comes

effects.log: {npc} says it has been winter for some time. You tell {him} you will know it when you see it.

events.text: A very old elder of {ctg_the} was once a child you pulled out of a river. They are dying, and they have made it their last act in the council to offer you a seat. {npc} has come to tell you, with the air of someone who thinks it is mad, and has been told to do it anyway. You remember the river. It was a good while ago, and you had not thought of it since. You were going somewhere else at the time.

choices.text: Go, while they can still see you sit down

effects.log: You get there in time. They are very small now. You sit in the chair, near the door, and they look across at you and they laugh, as far as they can.

choices.text: Send your thanks, and a jar of river water

effects.log: It is what you have. {npc} carries it back carefully. You do not hear what they said, and you do not ask.

events.text: Every side has been at war with every other at least twice in your lifetime, says {npc} of {ctg_the}, and you are the only thing in the jianghu that has stayed where it was. They would like to be able to say you are a friend. It would frighten the young. There is nothing in it for you, {he} says. It is why {he} thought you might.

choices.text: Let them say it

effects.log: It costs you nothing, you think. You remember thinking that about something else, a long while ago. Their silver comes each year, and you give it to a ferryman.

choices.text: Ask {him} which war {he} has in mind

effects.log: {He} tells you. You name the one it is really about, from two hundred years ago, and who started it, and {he} has never heard of any of them. You send {him} home to look it up.

events.text: You have held your rank longer than anyone living has held anything, says {npc} of {ctg_the}. You have seen five heads of that house come and go, and you have bowed to each of them. It must be a very comfortable thing to bow to children. They would be glad to have somebody like you to talk to, as a friend, now and then, about what those children are going to do.

choices.text: Talk to them, now and then

effects.log: You know these children. You knew their grandparents. It is the easiest thing in the world, and you do not like how easy it is.

choices.text: Say that you bowed because you meant it

effects.log: You did, for the first three or so. {npc} looks at you carefully, and {he} seems to have worked that out.

events.text: You have outlived the head of {ctg_the} who first proposed this friendship, and the one who revived it, and the one who took offence. {npc} has them all in {his} bag. It has become a kind of tradition, {he} explains, that each new head of the house should ask you. You have come to be a kind of rite of passage. {He} would be grateful for something different to tell them.

choices.text: Say yes, to see what happens

effects.log: Nobody knows what happens. There is no procedure. It takes them a whole year to work out what they have got, and your people find it very funny.

choices.text: Say what you said to the last one

effects.log: You remember it well. So does {he}. {He} writes it down under the others, with a sigh. It is not much of a rite if you never lose.

events.text: You have worn out four Grand Secretaries and a dynasty of astronomers. {npc} of {ctg_the} has come to your throne with an offer that was first made to your court before anyone now in it was born. The wording has not been changed. {He} reads it out. You find that you could say it along with {him}, and halfway through, you do. The whole court goes very quiet, because nobody knew that you could still do that.

choices.text: Grant it, this once, to reward the recital

effects.log: They could not have been more shocked if you had stood up and danced. You find it is worth it, just to see the Grand Secretary look it up.

choices.text: Finish the recital, and dismiss {him}

effects.log: You go on to the end, without {him}. Then you have {him} shown out. It will be another forty years before anyone there tries it again, and by that time you will have forgotten the last line.

events.text: {ctg_The} needs you to remember something. You are the last person alive who was there, says {npc}, and so whatever you say happened at the Plum Ford, ninety years ago, is what happened. There is some land in it. You do remember the Plum Ford, as it happens, and it is not what they would like. Nobody in the world can contradict you. You are starting to find that this is the most dangerous thing about being old.

choices.text: Remember it their way

effects.log: You remember it their way, in a clear voice. Nobody will ever know. You go home, and the real one is still there, and you are the only place it is kept.

choices.text: Say that it has all gone rather vague

effects.log: It has not. They do not believe you. It is an insult, and you are too old for them to do anything about that today.

choices.text: Tell them what happened, all of it

effects.log: You tell the hall, every word of it, and there are some people there who have built their whole lives on it having been otherwise. {npc} shuts {his} eyes.

events.text: All {ctg_the} wants is for you to be seen with their heir, walking slowly, somewhere public, with one hand on their arm. It need not be for long. You have reached the age, {npc} explains, at which you confer something. People are going to tell their grandchildren they saw it. {He} has found a very good garden for it, and {he} can have the crowd there by noon. Nobody asks how the arm will feel about it.

choices.text: Walk slowly, with a hand on the arm

effects.log: You walk. The heir is shaking a little. You say something to them that nobody else can hear, and it is not what the crowd thinks you said.

choices.text: Say that you have stopped going to gardens

effects.log: You go on not going. {npc} finds an old portrait and has it carried through the same garden. It is a great success, and nobody notices.

events.text: {npc} has come about {ctg_rival} again. You had thought that was finished. You finished it, you remember, for their great-grandparents, at a cost. It seems that they would like you to do that again, and there is a very young officer here with a map to show you how. {He} points out the ford. You could tell {him} who is buried at that ford, and who put them there. You look for your boots.

choices.text: Find your boots

effects.log: You go, and it goes as it went before. It is the same ford. It is exactly the same sort of morning, and they are all so young, on both sides.

choices.text: Tell them to find somebody who has not seen it

effects.log: There is nobody else, and that is why they came. You do not go. You think about that ford all of that year.

choices.text: Tell them it is over, for you, and for them

effects.log: You say it to the young officer. {He} looks very shocked, and then {he} rolls up the map. {npc} is older than {he} looks, and {he} goes outside for a little while.

events.text: {npc} of {ctg_the} has worked out who decides things in the house whose seal you hold for a child, and it is not the child. {He} speaks to you as one head of a house to another, and then, very carefully, as one who will not always be. A friendship between the houses: open roads, shared word of trouble, gifts at the New Year. "And when the child is grown," {he} adds, "a friend of ours will still be a friend of ours."

choices.text: Set the house's seal to it

effects.log: The seal goes down in the child's name and on your word. The elders read it twice and say nothing, and the house is now in a very old quarrel that nobody told you about.

choices.text: Say the seal is only lent to you

ok.log: {npc} bows as if that were the best answer {he} has heard this year. {He} writes it down. It will be read to the child one day, and it will sound well.

fail.log: {npc} says that a lent seal still makes a mark. {He} leaves you to think about whose.

choices.text: Say the house you keep for a child is not for sale while it is a child

effects.log: You say it in front of the elders. One of them nods. {npc} goes home and tells {ctg_head} that the house has a keeper, which they had not expected.

events.text: {npc} has brought two letters from {ctg_the}. One is for the child in the chair, very correct, with a gift of brushes. The other is for you. It offers a standing friendship, signed by the house you keep, and a place for you at their own table whenever the child comes of age and you are only yourself again. {He} lets you read both. {He} watches which one you read first.

choices.text: Sign for the house, and keep your letter

effects.log: You sign in the child's name. Your own letter goes into a drawer. You know exactly which drawer, and so, somehow, does {npc}.

choices.text: Give the child both letters

effects.log: The child reads them slowly, out loud, in front of the hall. It is the first thing they have ever decided. They decide no, and the elders look at you, and you let it stand.

choices.text: Say the child should be old enough to answer it

effects.log: {npc} says that {he} can wait for a child. {He} says it as if {he} has done it before.

events.text: It is the child they ask after first, which is clever of them. {npc} of {ctg_the} has heard that the young head is doing well at lessons, and wishes it to know that {ctg_the} would stand beside it, should anyone mistake a child in the chair for an empty chair. They would need only the seal. They understand it is in your keeping. They have always admired people who keep things well.

choices.text: Let them stand beside the child

effects.log: The friendship is written in the child's name. Nobody mistakes the chair for an empty one after that, and you are not sure whom the friendship is with.

choices.text: Say the child has you for that

effects.log: {npc} says that this is exactly what {he} was afraid of. {He} is very polite about it, and {he} leaves with your answer as if it were a gift.

choices.text: Say you will tell the child they asked

ok.log: You tell the child. The child asks what it means. You find you have to explain the whole murim, and it takes a week.

fail.log: {npc} asks if you will tell the child the answer too. It sounds like a question about you.

events.text: {npc} of {ctg_the} has come to ask the house whose seal you hold, and has found, as the last three envoys did, that you are still holding it. The child in the chair is not a child any more, in most of the ways that count. {He} would like to know, quietly, whether the house will say yes this time, or whether you will. {He} is fairly sure you know which of those {he} means.

choices.text: Say yes, for the house

effects.log: The seal goes down. The head of the house reads it later and does not object, which is either trust or something more patient.

choices.text: Say it is not yours to give for much longer

effects.log: {npc} writes that down with great care. Everyone at {ctg_the} will read it, and then everyone at the house you keep.
